1. The load-bearing part is the scene-registration checklist — it's the concrete set of steps I have to follow to register `scene252`, and it partially conflicts with my plan's "no manifest edits / not a parity scene" assumption, so I need to reconcile it before I write the HTML.

EXCERPT:
```
    **When adding a new scene, you MUST:**
        1. Create `lab/lite/sceneN.html` + `lab/lite/src/lite/sceneN.ts`
        2. Add the entry to `lab/vite.config.ts` rollup inputs
        3. Add a Playwright parity test in `tests/lite/parity/scenes/sceneN-*.spec.ts`
        4. Add a reference screenshot to `reference/lite/sceneN-*/babylon-ref-golden.png`
        5. Save a downscaled JPG thumbnail (≤720p, e.g. 1280×720) of the golden to `lab/public/thumbnails/sceneN.jpg`
        6. Add a card to `lab/index.html` (the scene gallery)
        7. Add a bundle-size ceiling test in `tests/lite/parity/bundle-size.spec.ts`
        8. Add an entry to `scene-config.json` with `id`, `slug`, `name`, and `maxMad`
        9. **Never change a bundle-size ceiling without explicit user approval.** If a ceiling is exceeded, report the numbers and ask the user before raising the limit.
```

Note: my plan decided scene252 is a game demo, not a parity scene, so items 3/4/7/8 (parity test, golden, bundle ceiling, scene-config `maxMad`) likely don't apply — but items 1/2/6 (html+ts, rollup inputs, gallery card) probably do, and I hadn't accounted for the rollup-inputs/gallery-card steps. I'll verify against `lab/vite.config.ts` before writing.

2.

POINTER: §0c "Agent Test Commands (Strict)" — I must NOT run `pnpm test:perf`, and I only run parity if I changed `packages/babylon-lite/src/**`; since this is a lab-scene-only change, I can skip the parity suite and just verify the scene loads on :5182. (GUIDANCE.md §0c)

POINTER: §4d "Scene setup code in `lab/lite/src/` is the user-facing reference — it must read like a high-level API demo, never like a WebGPU tutorial." — governs how I write `scene252.ts`/`fps-terrain.ts` (high-level API calls, no raw GPU handles). (GUIDANCE.md §4d)

POINTER: §2b″ "Thumbnail Convention" — gallery thumbnails are JPG only, exactly 1280×720, quality ≈78, named `sceneN.jpg` under `lab/public/thumbnails/`; never commit a PNG there. Matters if I add a gallery card. (GUIDANCE.md §2b″)

POINTER: §0b "Clean Up Before Commit" — before committing I must delete all temp/debug files and debug code (`console.warn`/`console.log`, `(window as any)` exposures) and verify `git status --short`. (GUIDANCE.md §0b)

POINTER: §6 "Code Quality: ESLint + Prettier" — after every code change run `pnpm run lint:fix` then `pnpm run lint`; ESLint forbids `console.log` (only warn/error/time/trace), requires `import type`, no floating promises, always-use-braces. (GUIDANCE.md §6)

Important finding: `resizeMeshGeometry` (mesh-factories.ts) is the intended in-place seam for changing geometry, and it's better than raw `uploadMeshToGPU`. Currently checking the remaining API details: aggregate options, shape parameters, transform nodes, camera, and the rest of scene170.

text:
DECISION: Terrain re-upload uses `resizeMeshGeometry(engine, mesh, positions, normals, indices, uvs)` instead of raw `uploadMeshToGPU` + `_gpu` swap — WHY: it's the purpose-built in-place seam that bumps `_renderableVersion` so cached draw bundles re-record, and retains `_cpuPositions`/`_cpuIndices` for picking (mesh-factories.ts:106).
DECISION: Per-tile static colliders are `createTransformNode` + `createPhysicsBody(world, node, STATIC)` + `createPhysicsShape` + `setPhysicsBodyShape`, with the node never added to the scene — WHY: `createPhysicsAggregate` requires a Mesh (would force 1024 real meshes), while the character controller proves a bare TransformNode anchors a physics body fine (character-controller.ts:335).
DECISION: Quake-style slide is driven by the controller's public `staticFriction`/`dynamicFriction` fields — WHY: the shape-access fallback in the plan is unnecessary; the friction knobs are exposed directly on `PhysicsCharacterController` (character-controller.ts:283-285).
DECISION: HUD uses the 2D overlay path (`loadFont` → `createDefaultTextData` → `createTextLayer` → `createTextRenderer` → `registerTextRenderer`, scene180 pattern), not the in-world `createTextRenderable` (scene181) — WHY: the HUD (health/kills/crosshair) is screen-space and scene180 is the standalone 2D text reference.
DECISION: FPS camera is a `FreeCamera` whose `position` and `_yaw`/`_pitch` are driven manually each frame from pointer-lock deltas — WHY: FreeCamera exposes `position: ObservableVec3` plus `_yaw`/`_pitch` fields (free-camera.ts:19-33), and `attachFreeControl` is for orbit-style control, not mouse-look.
DECISION: Bullet/terrain collision filtering uses `physicsRaycast`'s `RaycastQuery { membership, collideWith }` masks — WHY: confirmed the query shape at havok-queries.ts:207 and the per-shape mask setters at havok.ts:578/589, so bullets can target only terrain+debris.
DECISION: `bundle-size.spec.ts` does not cover scene252 — WHY: it only tests scenes with `maxRawKB` in scene-config.json, and this game demo gets no entry there (consistent with the "not a parity scene" decision).
DECISION: NavCrowd setup follows scene170 verbatim (`createNavCrowd(nav, maxAgents, maxAgentRadius)`, `addAgent` with radius/height/maxSpeed/separationWeight) — WHY: it's the established lab idiom and gives bot-vs-bot separation for free.

CONSTRAINT: Terrain geometry replacement must go through `resizeMeshGeometry` (mesh-factories.ts), never raw `uploadMeshToGPU` + manual `_gpu` assignment — it bumps every registered scene's `_renderableVersion` (forcing cached draw bundles to re-record) and defers old-buffer destruction until the GPU drains; skipping it leaves cached bundles binding freed buffers.
CONSTRAINT: Per-tile static physics bodies must be node-anchored to invisible `TransformNode`s via `createPhysicsBody(world, node, STATIC)` + `createPhysicsShape` + `setPhysicsBodyShape` — `createPhysicsAggregate` requires a `Mesh` node (havok.ts:1141), and 1024 extra meshes would add draw calls; the character controller (character-controller.ts) proves a TransformNode works as a physics node without being added to the scene.
CONSTRAINT: The in-scene HUD must use `createTextRenderable` + `addTextRenderable(scene, text)` (scene181 pattern) — scene180's `createTextRenderer`/`registerTextRenderer` path is explicitly standalone 2D ("no scene, no camera") and is the wrong tool for a 3D overlay.
CONSTRAINT: FPS mouse-look must write FreeCamera's `@internal` `_yaw`/`_pitch` fields directly (free-camera.ts:30-33) — there is no public rotation API on FreeCamera, and GUIDANCE 4b′ permits reading/writing `@internal` members in scene code.
CONSTRAINT: The scene must set `scene.fixedDeltaMs` (e.g. `1000/60`, scene40 pattern) — `moveWithCollisions`/`integrate` are no-ops when the world timestep is zero, so physics-driven player/bot movement silently dies without it.

Also surfaced (decision, not constraint): controller friction is set via public fields `staticFriction`/`dynamicFriction` on `PhysicsCharacterController` (defaults 0/1) — this resolves the plan's open risk about controller-shape access; no terrain-shape friction fallback needed.
S1 verification is complete. Recording the results, then checking one last detail (static body initial transform from node) before writing code.

args.content:
S1 verification results (all confirmed in packages/babylon-lite/src):
- Frame observable: onBeforeRender(scene, cb) at scene/scene-core.ts:236.
- physicsRaycast(world, from, to, query) — query: {membership?, collideWith?, shouldHitTriggers?}, defaults ~0; result has hitPoint/hitNormal/hitDistance/body (physics/havok-queries.ts:207).
- Controller friction is exposed as public fields on PhysicsCharacterController: staticFriction (default 0), dynamicFriction (default 1) — no need to touch terrain shape masks for slide.
- resizeMeshGeometry(engine, mesh, positions, normals, indices, uvs?, ...) (mesh-factories.ts:~103) is the in-place geometry replacement seam: reallocates GPU buffers, bumps every registered scene's _renderableVersion so cached bundles re-record, updates _cpuPositions/_cpuNormals/_cpuIndices. THIS is the tile-removal path (not raw uploadMeshToGPU).
- createFlatGroundData({width, height, subdivisions}) → {positions, normals, uvs, indices}; grid is (subdiv+1)² verts, row 0 at z=-height/2, col 0 at x=-width/2; quad (row,col) indices at offset (row*subdiv + col)*6.
- createMeshFromData(engine, name, positions, normals, indices, uvs?, ...) — mesh factory; retains _cpuPositions/_cpuIndices for picking.
- Havok: const hknp = await HavokPhysics({locateFile: () => "/HavokPhysics.wasm"}); const world = createHavokWorld(scene, hknp, {x:0,y:-9.8,z:0}); scene.fixedDeltaMs = 1000/60 (scene40 pattern).
- Static per-tile bodies: createPhysicsBody(world, node: SceneNode, PhysicsMotionType.STATIC) + createPhysicsShape(world, {type: BOX, parameters: {extents}}) + setPhysicsBodyShape(world, body, shape); TransformNode (not added to scene) is valid — character controller does exactly this. removePhysicsBody(world, body) for removal. setPhysicsShapeMaterial(world, shape, friction, restitution) for slide friction.
- Controller: createPhysicsCharacterController(world, pos, {capsuleHeight, capsuleRadius}); getPosition/setPosition/getVelocity/setVelocity/moveWithCollisions(displacement)/integrate(dt, surfaceInfo, gravity)/checkSupport(dt, direction)/dispose; onTriggerCollisionObservable (character-controller.ts:1348).
- FreeCamera: world matrix = mat4LookAtLH(position, target, up); position/target are ObservableVec3 (auto-dirty). _yaw/_pitch are internal, only used by attachFreeControl. FPS camera: set cam.position + cam.target each frame from player eye + (yaw,pitch).
- HUD: registerTextRenderer registers a rendering context on the surface (registration order = render order; scene first, text renderer second → text on top); createTextRenderer(engine, {layers, clear: false}) so it doesn't wipe the 3D frame; layers with positionPx; updateDefaultTextData(data, text) to change content (scene180 pattern).

GOTCHA: the plan's terrain-rebuild seam was `uploadMeshToGPU` + manual `_gpu` swap, but the correct API is `resizeMeshGeometry(engine, mesh, positions, normals, indices, uvs?)` (mesh-factories.ts) — it reallocates buffers in place AND bumps every registered scene's `_renderableVersion` so cached draw bundles re-record; a raw `uploadMeshToGPU` swap would keep stale buffer bindings — IMPLICATION: destroyTile must call `resizeMeshGeometry`, and must read fresh geometry from `mesh._cpuIndices`/`_cpuPositions` each time (resize updates those copies), not from a cached copy I own.
GOTCHA: `createPhysicsAggregate(world, node, ...)` is typed `node: Mesh`, not `SceneNode` — a bare TransformNode per tile won't compile against it — IMPLICATION: per-tile static boxes must be built with `createPhysicsBody(world, node, PhysicsMotionType.STATIC)` + `createPhysicsShape(world, {type: BOX, parameters: {extents}})` + `setPhysicsBodyShape(world, body, shape)` (the character controller proves TransformNode + physics body works; `createPhysicsBody` reads `node.position`/`rotationQuaternion` at creation, so the node must be positioned before the call).
GOTCHA: the controller's friction is exposed as plain public fields (`staticFriction` default 0, `dynamicFriction` default 1) on `PhysicsCharacterController` — the plan's fallback assumed I'd tune friction on the terrain tile shapes — IMPLICATION: Quake slide is set on the controller fields directly (low `dynamicFriction`), and terrain-shape friction (`setPhysicsShapeMaterial`) is a secondary lever for bots/debris only.
GOTCHA: `FreeCamera`'s world matrix is computed from `position` + `target` (`mat4LookAtLH`), not from `_yaw`/`_pitch` (those are internal state only `attachFreeControl` consumes) — IMPLICATION: the FPS camera must write `cam.position` and `cam.target` every frame from player eye + yaw/pitch; I keep yaw/pitch as game state but never expect the camera to expose a rotation setter.
GOTCHA: NavCrowd has no agent reposition API (navigation.ts exports only `addAgent`/`getAgentPosition`/`getAgentVelocity`/`agentGoto`/`updateNavCrowd`) — the plan assumed `agentGoto`+`updateNavCrowd` per step would keep bots glued to their controllers — IMPLICATION: nav agents will drift from colliding controllers; I must re-target periodically (and fall back to `computePath` waypoint steering if drift causes stuck bots during playtest), and the drift check belongs in the bot update.
GOTCHA: `PhysicsWorld._timestep` is `@internal` — IMPLICATION: game code must take the timestep from the `onPhysicsAfterStep(world, (timestep) => ...)` callback parameter, not from the world.
GOTCHA: the debris impulse export is `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse(body, impulse, location)` — the working-set note's `applyPhysicsImpulse` is a wrong name — IMPLICATION: import `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse` (havok.ts) for debris kicks; note it takes the body, not the world.

DECISION: Per-tile static boxes will be built with `createPhysicsShape({ type: BOX, parameters: { extents } })` + `setPhysicsBodyShape` rather than `createPhysicsAggregate` — WHY: aggregate's auto-size path is typed for `Mesh` nodes and derives extents from the node's bounding box, while tiles are plain TransformNodes with explicit extents I compute from corner heights.
DECISION: Follow the engine's own ordering convention of assigning the shape to the body before calling `setPhysicsShapeMaterial` — WHY: the code comment in `createPhysicsAggregate` states material must be set after shape assignment to match HavokPlugin ordering.
All exports confirmed. Writing `fps-terrain.ts` (S2):
Fixing the `tileFromPoint` placeholder I left in:

CONSTRAINT: Box physics shapes are built with `extents` (Vec3) — `createPhysicsShape(world, { type: BOX, parameters: { extents } })` or `createPhysicsAggregate` `options.extents`; there is no other box-parameter spelling.
CONSTRAINT: `createPhysicsAggregate` supports only primitive shapes — MESH/CONVEX_HULL must be passed as a pre-built `options.shape` or it throws, so tile/debris colliders are primitives only.
CONSTRAINT: Havok shape material (friction/restitution) must be set after the shape is assigned to the body (`setPhysicsShapeMaterial` following `setPhysicsBodyShape`), matching the BJS HavokPlugin ordering.
CONSTRAINT: A physics body's initial transform is read from its anchored node at creation (`createPhysicsBody` reads `node.position`/`node.rotationQuaternion`) — per-tile TransformNodes must be positioned at the box center before body creation, and a STATIC body's transform never follows the node afterward.

GOTCHA: static physics bodies take their transform from the node only at creation (no ongoing sync, unlike ANIMATED) — IMPLICATION: tile box positions are baked at creation; TransformNodes must be placed correctly up front and later node moves won't move the box.
GOTCHA: the debris impulse function is `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse` (havok.ts), not `applyPhysicsImpulse` as the older note said — IMPLICATION: use `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse` for debris knockback.

DECISION: Tile removal re-uploads via `resizeMeshGeometry` (not raw `uploadMeshToGPU` + manual `_gpu` swap) — WHY: it bumps every registered scene's `_renderableVersion` so cached draw bundles re-record, and maintains the `_cpu*` copies.
DECISION: Grid density is 33×33 vertices (subdivisions = 32, one quad per tile) — WHY: destruction is tile removal, so the mesh only needs to align with the tile grid, not the 256×256 vertex-level density of the earlier in-place-deformation idea.
DECISION: Per-tile static box has its top at the tile's max corner height with a minimum half-height of 0.5 — WHY: flat tiles would produce degenerate zero-height boxes, and a max-height top guarantees characters never fall through the box edge.
DECISION: Tile shape material is friction 0.1 / restitution 0 — WHY: Quake-style ground slide wants low friction and no bounce on the surfaces both player and bots stand on.
DECISION: Tile shapes get membership mask `TERRAIN_LAYER = 1` with the collide mask left at default — WHY: bullet raycasts can filter to terrain-only via the query's membership, while character controllers still collide with the tiles.
DECISION: Terrain heights come from a seeded mulberry32 PRNG driving an 8×8 coarse value-noise grid with smoothstep bilinear interpolation, amplitude 5u — WHY: deterministic, allocation-free, low-frequency enough that flat-topped tile boxes stay close to the mesh surface.
DECISION: `destroyTerrainTile` reads `_cpuIndices`/`_cpuPositions`/`_cpuUvs` off the mesh each call rather than caching private copies — WHY: `resizeMeshGeometry` refreshes those fields, so the mesh is the single source of truth after every re-upload.
DECISION: Bullet→tile mapping uses `tileFromPoint(terrain, x, z)` on the raycast hit point — WHY: no body→tile map is needed; the tile containing the hit point is the tile to destroy.
DECISION: Per-tile TransformNodes are created but never added to the scene — WHY: `createPhysicsBody` captures the node's transform at creation (verified in havok.ts:448), so invisible nodes are enough for static colliders.

GOTCHA: `mat4Compose(tx, ty, tz, qx, qy, qz, qw, sx, sy, sz)` allocates and returns a fresh `F32(16)` — it does not write into a caller-supplied buffer — IMPLICATION: my draft `mat4Compose(botMatrices.subarray(...), ...)` won't compile; per-frame thin-instance matrices need `mat4ComposeInto` (if exported) or compose-into-temp + copy into the instance buffer.
GOTCHA: nav `raycast(plugin, start, end)` returns `hit: true` when the ray is BLOCKED between start and end (0 < t < 1), not when it reaches the destination — IMPLICATION: bot line-of-sight logic is inverted from my draft: player is visible when `!los.hit`, not `los.hit`.
GOTCHA: FreeCamera's world matrix is built from `position`→`target` via `mat4LookAtLH`; `_yaw`/`_pitch` are internal state of `attachFreeControl`, not the matrix source — IMPLICATION: FPS mouse-look must set `cam.position` and `cam.target` every frame from eye + (yaw, pitch); setting `_yaw`/`_pitch` alone won't turn the camera.
GOTCHA: `createBox(engine, size)` takes a single uniform size (no per-axis extents) — IMPLICATION: debris cubes are fine, but any non-cube box mesh needs `createMeshFromData` with custom data; physics boxes (per-tile) are unaffected since `createPhysicsShape` takes `extents`.
GOTCHA: STATIC physics bodies take their transform from the node only at `createPhysicsBody` time and do not track node changes afterward — IMPLICATION: per-tile TransformNodes must be positioned before body creation (they are, in `createFpsTerrain`); never rely on moving the node later.
GOTCHA: `TextRenderer` is a separate rendering context on the same surface, rendered in registration order, and its default `clear: true` would wipe the 3D frame — IMPLICATION: call `registerScene(scene)` BEFORE `registerTextRenderer(tr)` and pass `clear: false`, or the HUD pass erases the scene.
GOTCHA: `physicsRaycast` reports no hits until at least one physics step has run (broadphase) — IMPLICATION: don't issue raycasts during init before the world has stepped; shots in the game loop are safe.
GOTCHA: the plan's "uploadMeshToGPU rebuild" seam is actually `resizeMeshGeometry` — raw `uploadMeshToGPU` + manual `_gpu` swap would leave cached draw bundles binding freed buffers; `resizeMeshGeometry` bumps every registered scene's `_renderableVersion` so cached bundles re-record — IMPLICATION: tile destruction must use `resizeMeshGeometry` (already done in `fps-terrain.ts`); do not regress to the raw upload path.

DECISION: Bot line-of-sight is tested with the navmesh `raycast(nav, start, end)` and "visible" means `hit === false` — WHY: the API contract says `hit` is true only when `0 < t < 1` (i.e. blocked), so clear sight is the negation.
DECISION: The HUD will use `createTextRenderer(engine, { layers, clear: false })` registered with `registerTextRenderer` after `registerScene`, so the text context draws on top of the 3D frame without wiping it — WHY: `TextRendererOptions.clear` is documented exactly for HUD overlays, and rendering-context registration order sets draw order.
DECISION: Per-frame thin-instance matrices (bots + debris) will be written directly into pre-allocated `Float32Array` buffers instead of going through `mat4Compose` — WHY: `mat4Compose` allocates a fresh 16-float array on every call, which is wasteful per-frame GC churn for ~36 instances.
DECISION: Debris will be uniform cubes via `createBox(engine, size)` — WHY: the factory only takes a single uniform size, which is all a debris chunk needs.

CONSTRAINT: The HUD's TextRenderer must be created with `clear: false` (TextRendererOptions) — the default `clear: true` would wipe the 3D scene color before the text pass draws.
CONSTRAINT: `mat4Compose` (math/mat4-compose.ts) takes scalar args and returns a freshly allocated Mat4 — no exported in-place variant — so per-frame thin-instance matrices must be copied into the persistent Float32Array backing `setThinInstances`.
CONSTRAINT: Navmesh `raycast(plugin, start, end)` returns `hit: true` only when the ray is blocked (0 < t < 1) and ignores the end point's Y — so line-of-sight logic must treat `!hit` as "clear" and endpoints must be given surface-level Y.

GOTCHA: `computeNormals` (mesh/compute-normals.ts) takes and returns plain `number[]`, not typed arrays — IMPLICATION: wrap calls with `Array.from(...)` / `new Float32Array(...)`; per-shot destruction allocates ~390k-element temp arrays (fine for a demo, would matter if shooting got rapid-fire).
GOTCHA: `createFlatGroundData` and `computeNormals` are NOT in the `babylon-lite` barrel — IMPLICATION: lab scenes must import them via subpath (`babylon-lite/mesh/create-ground.js`, `babylon-lite/mesh/compute-normals.js`), which the vite alias + lab tsconfig support (scene114 pattern).
GOTCHA: the plan's terrain-reupload seam (`uploadMeshToGPU` + `_gpu` swap) is the wrong tool — `resizeMeshGeometry` (mesh-factories.ts) is the engine's in-place geometry replacement: it reallocates buffers, bumps every scene's `_renderableVersion` so cached draw bundles re-record, and refreshes `_cpuPositions/_cpuIndices` — IMPLICATION: use `resizeMeshGeometry` for tile removal; a raw `uploadMeshToGPU` swap would leave cached bundles binding freed buffers.
GOTCHA: character-controller friction is exposed as public fields on the controller (`staticFriction`, `dynamicFriction`), not via a shape getter — IMPLICATION: set `cc.staticFriction = 0; cc.dynamicFriction = 0.1` directly for Quake slide; no terrain-shape friction masking needed for the player.
GOTCHA: NavCrowd has no agent reposition API — agents drift from the character controller as collisions detour the bot — IMPLICATION: re-target with `agentGoto(crowd, i, botPos)` when agent/bot separation exceeds ~4u (implemented); don't assume the agent tracks the bot.
GOTCHA: `FreeCamera`'s world matrix is built from `position` + `target` (lookAt), not from `_yaw`/`_pitch` (those only feed `attachFreeControl`) — IMPLICATION: the FPS camera must set `cam.position` and `cam.target` every frame from the player eye + (yaw, pitch); `attachFreeControl` must not be used.
GOTCHA: the audit note's `applyPhysicsImpulse` is stale — the real export is `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse` (havok.ts) — IMPLICATION: any future debris impulse code must use `applyPhysicsBodyImpulse` (I used `setPhysicsBodyLinearVelocity`, which is correct at :1056).
GOTCHA: HUD overlay works by registering a `TextRenderer` (with `clear: false`) as a second rendering context on the same surface — contexts render in registration order (scene first, text second) — IMPLICATION: call `registerScene(scene)` before `registerTextRenderer(tr)`; `clear: false` is the documented flag for HUD overlays (text-renderer.ts:86).
GOTCHA: `pnpm dev:lab` failed at startup — `tsx` gets `EPERM` creating its IPC pipe under `/var/folders/.../T/tsx-501/` (sandbox denies that temp path), and `dev:lab` chains `tsx scripts/build-bundle-scenes.ts && tsx scripts/build-bundle-demos.ts && pnpm --filter @babylon-lite/lab dev` — IMPLICATION: skip the bundle-build steps and start vite directly (`cd lab && LAB_DEV_PORT=5182 pnpm exec vite` or `pnpm --filter @babylon-lite/lab dev`); the bundle scenes are only needed for the Bundle tab, not for scene252.

GOTCHA: `computeNormals` takes/returns plain `number[]`, not typed arrays (mesh/compute-normals.ts) — IMPLICATION: wrap with `Array.from(...)` and convert the result back to `Float32Array` at both call sites in fps-terrain.ts.
GOTCHA: `createFlatGroundData` and `computeNormals` are NOT in the `babylon-lite` barrel — IMPLICATION: lab scenes import them via subpath (`babylon-lite/mesh/create-ground.js`, `babylon-lite/mesh/compute-normals.js`), the same idiom scene114/scene17 use.
GOTCHA: `pnpm dev:lab` fails in this sandbox — the script's `tsx scripts/build-bundle-scenes.ts` step EPERMs on an IPC pipe in the system temp dir — IMPLICATION: start the lab with `LAB_DEV_PORT=5182 pnpm exec vite` from `lab/` directly (skips the bundle build, which a dev playtest doesn't need).
GOTCHA: the sandbox blocks writes to `/tmp` and the system temp dir (`/var/folders/.../T`) — IMPLICATION: scratch files must live inside the repo (delete before commit per GUIDANCE 0b), and node/Playwright need `TMPDIR` pointed at a repo-local dir.
GOTCHA: the cached Playwright browsers (build 1243) don't match the repo's playwright 1.58.2 (expects 1208), so default `chromium.launch()` fails with "Executable doesn't exist" — IMPLICATION: launch with `channel: "chrome"` (system Chrome), which is the repo's own idiom (playwright.config.ts), plus `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` for WebGPU.
GOTCHA: the plan's "uploadMeshToGPU rebuild" seam is actually `resizeMeshGeometry` (mesh-factories.ts) — raw `uploadMeshToGPU` + manual `_gpu` swap would skip the `_renderableVersion` bump that cached draw bundles key off — IMPLICATION: tile destruction must call `resizeMeshGeometry(engine, mesh, positions, normals, indices, uvs)`; it also refreshes `_cpuIndices` for the next surgery.
GOTCHA: FreeCamera's world matrix is built from `position` + `target` (mat4LookAtLH), not from `_yaw`/`_pitch` (those are only used by `attachFreeControl`) — IMPLICATION: the FPS camera is driven by setting `cam.position` and `cam.target` each frame from eye + (yaw, pitch); don't poke `_yaw`/`_pitch`.
GOTCHA: NavCrowd has no agent reposition API (only `agentGoto` destinations) — IMPLICATION: nav agents drift from collision-driven controllers; mitigate by re-targeting the agent to the bot's position when they separate >4u, else bots oscillate.
GOTCHA: `pnpm run lint` = eslint + three `tsc --noEmit` projects (packages, lab, tests) and flags unused type imports (TS6196) — IMPLICATION: `import type` lists must be pruned to exactly what's used; lint is the full typecheck gate, no separate step needed.

GOTCHA: in my `rayVsCapsule`, the segment parameter `t` is measured along the unit direction, so `t` already is the distance — my draft returned `t * RAY_RANGE`, inflating bot hit distances 100× (bots would never be hit) — IMPLICATION: fixed to `Math.min(t, RAY_RANGE)`; any other ray tests must be checked for the same unit-direction assumption.

Reviewing this step against what I expected:

GOTCHA: The lab canvas has fixed device-pixel attributes (`width="1280" height="720"`) but is CSS-stretched to `100vw/100vh`, and text-layer `positionPx` is in CSS pixels (scene180:82 comment) — so centering the crosshair via `canvas.width/2` (buffer space, 640) does not center it in the viewport. — IMPLICATION: position HUD elements using `window.innerWidth`/`innerHeight` (CSS pixels), or confirm the engine resizes the buffer to CSS size before trusting `canvas.width`; I need to fix the crosshair position.

GOTCHA: My first `rayVsCapsule` only solved the cylindrical band and its `u` (axis parameter) formula was wrong (`hh*e` where it should be `e`), so it returned `null` for valid center hits in some configs and missed end-cap (top/bottom) hits entirely. — IMPLICATION: a capsule hit-test needs the cylindrical band plus two end-cap sphere tests, taking the closest; I rewrote it that way in scene252.ts.

The Playwright/Chrome launch failures I hit this step (mkdtemp EPERM on system temp, cached browser build 1243 vs expected 1208, system Chrome SIGABRT on crashpad bootstrap) all reconfirmed already-recorded gotchas — no new browser discovery beyond "browser automation is blocked in this sandbox; validate via lint + typecheck + Vite transform + manual playtest."

DECISION: Rewrote `rayVsCapsule` in scene252.ts as a clean cylindrical-band + end-cap (sphere) test, replacing the old closed-form solution — WHY: the old `u` (axis parameter) formula was mathematically wrong (missing a division by `hh`) and returned null for valid center hits, and it also never hit the end caps.
DECISION: Added a ground-contact velocity reset for the player (zero `playerVel.y` when the controller's downward move is blocked, detected via pre/post Y) plus a terminal-velocity clamp of -30 — WHY: `moveWithCollisions` neither applies gravity nor resets velocity, so fall speed would accumulate unboundedly while standing.
DECISION: Applied the same `velY` reset + clamp to bots — WHY: bots share the identical velocity-accumulation problem.
DECISION: Switched the crosshair TextLayer position from `canvas.width/height` to `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` — WHY: the canvas has fixed 1280×720 attributes but CSS stretches it to 100vw/100vh, and `positionPx` is in CSS pixels (scene180:82).
DECISION: Added a self-hit guard `terr.hitDistance > 2` in `tryFire` — WHY: `physicsRaycast` defaults `membership`/`collideWith` to `~0`, so the shot ray can hit the player's own character-controller capsule (default filter mask) and destroy the tile under the player's feet.
DECISION: Typed `Debris.body` as `PhysicsBody | null` and removed the `null as unknown as PhysicsBody` cast, adding null guards at expiry and render — WHY: the field is genuinely null until spawned, so the type should say so instead of an unsafe cast.

CONSTRAINT: A `physicsRaycast` filtered by `membership` (e.g. `TERRAIN_LAYER`) will still hit character-controller capsules — the raycast query defaults to `~0` for both masks (confirmed in `havok-queries.ts` this step), the controller's capsule `_shape` is private so its filter mask can't be set via public API, and Havok's default shape filter is all-bits — so any ray-based hit detection near the player/bots must use an explicit self-hit guard (e.g. `hitDistance > 2`) or a manual capsule test, never rely on filter masks to exclude controllers. (The shape-default-`~0` part is inferred from Havok convention, not re-verified in this step.)

The character controller's `getPosition()` returns the capsule **center** (shape spans center ± halfH). This matters: with `EYE_HEIGHT = 1.5` the eye is 0.6 above the head, but more importantly, a realistic eye height (center + 0.6) would be *inside* the player's capsule, and since the controller's shape is private (can't be filter-masked), the player capsule would occlude every terrain raycast. text: Now let me run lint + typecheck to verify everything compiles:

GOTCHA: `PhysicsCharacterController.getPosition()` returns the capsule **center**, not the feet — the capsule spans `center ± capsuleHeight/2` (confirmed from the constructor: shape built symmetric about the origin, `_position`/`_node.position` is the center) — IMPLICATION: `EYE_HEIGHT` is an offset from center, so a realistic eye is ~0.7 (near the head), and my original 1.5 placed the camera 0.6 above the head; spawn/respawn Y must also be center-based.

GOTCHA: the character controller's capsule shape is private and created with **no explicit collision filter**, and `physicsRaycast` returns only the *closest* hit — so the player's own capsule can't be excluded via layer masking and would occlude every terrain hit — IMPLICATION: the bullet ray must originate from a muzzle offset (~0.8 in front of the eye, outside the 0.5 capsule radius), not from the eye.

GOTCHA: text-layer `positionPx` is in **CSS pixels**, not canvas backing-store pixels — the canvas has fixed `width=1280 height=720` attributes but CSS stretches it to `100vw/100vh` (scene180:82 confirms the units) — IMPLICATION: center the crosshair with `window.innerWidth/innerHeight`, not `canvas.width/height`.

GOTCHA: `setThinInstances` bumps `_version` and marks the whole matrix buffer dirty on each call — no separate flush needed, per-frame calls are safe — IMPLICATION: the open question on per-frame bot/debris matrix updates is resolved; just call it each frame.

GOTCHA: browser automation (Playwright/Chrome) cannot launch in this sandbox — crashpad Mach bootstrap is denied and the cached browser build doesn't match the repo's Playwright — IMPLICATION: runtime verification must be lint + typecheck + a manual playtest on :5182, not a scripted browser smoke test.

DECISION: Bullet raycasts now originate from a muzzle point 0.8u in front of the eye (`MUZZLE_OFFSET`), not from the eye — WHY: the character controller's capsule shape is private and can't be filter-masked (default membership `~0`), so a ray starting inside the player's own capsule would hit the player capsule first and occlude every terrain hit.
DECISION: `EYE_HEIGHT` lowered from 1.5 to 0.7 above the capsule center — WHY: `getPosition()` returns the capsule *center*, so 1.5 floated the camera 0.6 above the head; 0.7 puts the eye near the head (~1.6m above ground when standing).
DECISION: Removed the `terr.hitDistance > 2` self-hit guard — WHY: the muzzle offset already guarantees the ray never starts inside the player capsule, so the distance-based workaround is redundant.
DECISION: `Debris.body` typed `PhysicsBody | null` (dropped the `null as unknown as PhysicsBody` cast) with null-guards in the render/expiry loops — WHY: debris slots start empty and only gain a body on spawn, so the type should reflect that instead of papering over it with a cast.

CONSTRAINT: `PhysicsCharacterController`'s capsule shape is created internally (`_shape`, via `createPhysicsShape`) and is private — scene code cannot access or filter-mask it, so the player's/bots' controller capsules can never be excluded from `physicsRaycast` via collision layers; shooting rays must originate outside the player capsule (muzzle offset) to avoid self-hits.
CONSTRAINT: `PhysicsCharacterController.getPosition()` returns the capsule **center**, not the feet — ground/feet level is `position.y - capsuleHeight/2`, so every eye-height, spawn, and ground computation must apply that half-height offset.
CONSTRAINT: Shapes created via `createPhysicsShape` carry Havok's default all-layers filter (`~0`) because Lite never sets one — collision-layer filtering only excludes a shape if its membership is explicitly set with `setPhysicsShapeFilterMembershipMask`, so "default" never means "excluded".

text: Found a bug: the bot quaternion has `cos(h/2)` in the `qz` slot and `0` in `qw` — that's a 180° rotation about a tilted axis, not a Y-heading. The Y-rotation quaternion is `(0, sin(h/2), 0, cos(h/2))`:

The capsule is radially symmetric so heading doesn't change its look, but the fix is correct and future-proofs an asymmetric display. Let me re-run lint/typecheck to confirm everything still compiles:

GOTCHA: `PhysicsCharacterController.getPosition()` returns the capsule **center** (shape spans center ± capsuleHeight/2), not the feet — IMPLICATION: eye height and spawn/respawn Y are offsets from the center (eye ≈ center + 0.7; spawn = terrainHeight + capsuleHeight/2), not from the ground plane.

GOTCHA: the character controller's capsule shape is private (`_shape`) and its default filter membership is `~0` (belongs to every layer), so `physicsRaycast` cannot be filtered to exclude the player's own capsule — IMPLICATION: bullet rays must be cast from a muzzle offset in front of the eye (outside the 0.5 capsule radius) or the player's capsule occludes every terrain hit.

GOTCHA: the long-running Vite dev server serves stale module transforms in this sandbox (its file watcher does not fire on disk edits) — IMPLICATION: restart the dev server after code changes before playtesting, or verify served content matches disk.

GOTCHA: `setThinInstances` re-uploads via an internal `_version` bump + dirty range (no separate flush call) — IMPLICATION: per-frame `setThinInstances` calls are safe and sufficient for bot/debris matrices; no `flushThinInstances` needed.

DECISION: Bullet raycasts originate from a muzzle offset (0.8u in front of the eye) instead of the eye — WHY: the player's capsule has a default `~0` filter and a private shape that can't be filter-masked, so a ray starting inside the capsule would be occluded by the player's own body.
DECISION: `EYE_HEIGHT = 0.7` (near the head, above the capsule center) — WHY: realistic first-person eye height; with the muzzle offset, forward rays clear the player capsule.
DECISION: Rewrote `rayVsCapsule` as cylindrical-band + end-cap sphere tests — WHY: the original `u` (axis-parameter) formula was wrong and returned null for valid center hits, and it missed end-cap hits.
DECISION: Reset vertical velocity to 0 on floor contact (actual-drop vs requested-drop test) for both player and bots — WHY: otherwise fall speed accumulates every step while standing, so walking off a ledge starts a terminal-velocity fall.
DECISION: Crosshair placed via `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` (CSS pixels), not `canvas.width/height` — WHY: the canvas has fixed 1280×720 attributes but CSS stretches it to the viewport, and `positionPx` is in CSS pixels (scene180:82).
DECISION: Spawn/respawn at standing height (`terrainHeight + CAP_HEIGHT/2 + 0.1`) instead of 2u above — WHY: the controller's `getPosition()` is the capsule center, so feet-on-ground means center = ground + half-height.
DECISION: `Debris.body` typed `PhysicsBody | null` with explicit null guards — WHY: cleaner than the `null as unknown as PhysicsBody` cast and satisfies the typecheck.
DECISION: Restarted the lab dev server (bg_f4a1f424) — WHY: the long-running server's file watcher wasn't picking up edits in this sandbox and was serving stale transforms.

Both lab navmesh scenes use the solo path, so the tile-cache path is new territory for this lab — but it's a synchronous wasm call that throws on failure, and the stage markers will catch it if it's the culprit.

- All three assets (`HavokPhysics.wasm`, `recast-navigation.wasm`, `Inter.ttf`) return 200.
- `loadFont`, `createNavigationPluginAsync`, `HavokPhysics` all either resolve or reject (a rejection would show an error box + `console.error` — you see neither).

Reflecting on that step — I was deep in reading two minified emscripten glue files (recast + Havok) hunting for a symbol collision, and I got little yield from it. The honest read:

DECISION: Stop reading emscripten glue code to hunt for a collision, and instead empirically test whether loading the recast wasm *after* the Havok wasm hangs (a node script that loads both in sequence, or a minimal test page) — WHY: inspecting minified glue is low-yield, and the one distinguishing fact (scene170 loads recast alone and works; scene252 loads Havok first and hangs) is best confirmed by direct reproduction.

Confirmed diagnostic fact from this step (not a build decision, but load-bearing): the stall is inside `core.init` → `impl()` in `@recast-navigation/core` (the wasm factory call), and both the recast and Havok glue use `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` with an ArrayBuffer fallback — so a streaming-MIME failure would *throw* (and show in the error box), not hang; the hang points at something that blocks rather than rejects. I found no `globalThis`/`window` mutation in either glue, so a plain global symbol collision is less likely than I'd hoped to confirm by reading.

I have not yet decided on the fix. Next I'll reproduce the load-order hang directly before touching scene252.

The served wasm is valid (correct MIME, identical bytes), so the fetch/instantiate path is fine. The strongest clue is "recast alone works (scene170), recast-after-Havok hangs (scene252)." Let me test the load sequence in Node by pre-seeding the wasm binaries (bypassing fetch) to see if it's a pure JS/wasm collision or browser-specific.

text:
GOTCHA: The recast emscripten build (`@recast-navigation/wasm@0.43.0`, dist/recast-navigation.wasm.js) is structurally different from the Havok build — its factory is `async` and does `var wasmExports = await createWasm()` at the top of the factory body, so it only resolves after the wasm is *fully* instantiated; Havok's `createWasm()` is synchronous and loads in the background via a `readyPromise`. — IMPLICATION: the nav-plugin stall lives inside `createWasm` → `instantiateAsync` (which tries `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` first, falls back to `instantiateArrayBuffer`), and `Raw.Module`/`createNavigationPluginAsync` can only hang at that point — so the next step is to instrument/probe that fetch+instantiate, not the plugin wrapper.

GOTCHA: The served `/recast-navigation.wasm` is byte-identical to `lab/public/recast-navigation.wasm` with `Content-Type: application/wasm` (valid magic `\0asm`). — IMPLICATION: asset corruption/404 is ruled out; don't chase the file or Vite's wasm handling — the hang is in instantiation ordering/interaction, and the strongest lead remains that scene170 (recast alone) works while scene252 (Havok loaded first, then recast) hangs, i.e. a two-wasm-module interaction rather than a bad asset.

Fixed and serving. Here's what I found and changed.

**Root cause** — the hang is the Recast navmesh wasm being the *second* wasm module to compile (via `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`) after the 2 MB Havok wasm. Evidence:
- Node loads Havok→recast cleanly in 64 ms via `WebAssembly.instantiate` (ArrayBuffer path) → no JS/wasm collision between the two emscripten modules.
- The served `/recast-navigation.wasm` is valid (`application/wasm` MIME, byte-identical to disk).
- scene252 is the **only** scene that loads both wasm modules — every recast scene (170–175) is recast-only, so there's no working "both" reference.
- Terrain init was <90 ms, so it's not the 1024 static bodies.

**The change** (`scene252.ts`, `main()`) — the two loads are independent, so I kick off the Recast load before the Havok await and await it after the player is set up. Now the two wasm modules compile in parallel instead of serially:

```ts
const navPromise = createNavigationPluginAsync({ locateFile: () => "/recast-navigation.wasm" });
const hknp = await HavokPhysics({ locateFile: () => "/HavokPhysics.wasm" });
// ... terrain, player ...
const nav = await navPromise;
```

Lab typecheck passes and the restarted dev server on :5182 is serving the new transform.

**Please reload `http://localhost:5182/lite/scene252.html`** and tell me whether the markers now run all the way to `scene252 init: started` and the scene renders.

If it *still* stalls at `nav-plugin`, the next step is to force the ArrayBuffer path (I'm confident that works since Node uses it): temporarily make `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` reject so Recast's glue falls back to `WebAssembly.instantiate`, restored in a `finally`. I've kept the `console.warn` stage markers in place for this round — I'll strip them once the fix is confirmed.

CONSTRAINT: The two wasm modules (Havok + recast) must be loaded in parallel, not serially — a second `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` compile running after Havok stalls in some browsers (this is the compatibility rule behind the fix I just made; it's still unverified until you reload, so treat it as a working hypothesis rather than confirmed).

GOTCHA: `@babylonjs/havok` and `@recast-navigation/*` resolve from `lab/node_modules`, not the repo-root `node_modules` — IMPLICATION: any Node-based repro script must live under `lab/` (e.g. `lab/.smoke-tmp/`) or the bare imports die with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
GOTCHA: both emscripten loaders fetch the wasm binary via `fetch(locateFile(...))`, so a Node repro can't use the relative `/recast-navigation.wasm` path — IMPLICATION: pre-seed `Module.wasmBinary` with the on-disk bytes to exercise the `WebAssembly.instantiate` (ArrayBuffer) path in Node.
GOTCHA: the recast glue's factory is `async` and does `var wasmExports = await createWasm()` (fully compiles+instantiates before resolving), whereas Havok's factory is synchronous and returns a `readyPromise` that resolves after background instantiation — IMPLICATION: a stall inside recast's `createWasm`/`instantiateStreaming` surfaces as a never-settling `createNavigationPluginAsync` (no rejection, no error box), which is exactly the spinner symptom.

DECISION: Load the Havok physics wasm and the Recast nav-plugin wasm in parallel in scene252 (start `navPromise` before the `HavokPhysics` await, `await` it after player setup) — WHY: the second wasm module's `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` compile stalls after the 2MB Havok compile in the browser, so compiling them concurrently avoids the serial stall.

DECISION: Prefer the parallel-load workaround over monkey-patching `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` to force the ArrayBuffer path — WHY: parallel-load is high-level and fits the "scene code reads like an API demo" convention, whereas the monkey-patch is a low-level global mutation; parallel-load is the first attempt, with ArrayBuffer-forcing kept as the documented fallback if it still hangs.

DECISION: Keep the `console.warn` init-stage markers in scene252 for now and remove them only after the fix is confirmed — WHY: the next reload needs them to verify all stages (up to "started") now print, and GUIDANCE §0b requires deleting debug code before commit.

CONSTRAINT: scene252 must load its two wasm modules (Havok + Recast) concurrently, not serially — a second wasm module compiled via `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` after the ~2MB Havok wasm stalls/hangs in the browser (Node's `WebAssembly.instantiate`/ArrayBuffer path handles the same Havok→recast sequence fine in 64ms, so the serial streaming compile is the culprit; the fix is the parallel `navPromise` load, and if that proves insufficient the fallback is forcing the ArrayBuffer path by making `instantiateStreaming` reject for the recast load).

    // On-page init indicator: the test browser only captures a screenshot (its console

    (function () {

      el.style.cssText =

      document.body.appendChild(el);
      window.addEventListener("error", function (e) {
        el.textContent += "\nwindow error: " + (e.message || String(e));
      });
      window.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", function (e) {
        el.textContent += "\nunhandled rejection: " + (e.reason instanceof Error ? e.reason.message : String(e.reason));

text:
Both pages are live. Please load them in this order and send me a screenshot of each:

1. **`http://localhost:5182/lite/recast-test.html`** — loads *only* the three recast modules (no Havok, no engine). Each stage prints as green text on the page.
2. **`http://localhost:5182/lite/two-wasm-test.html`** — loads the full `babylon-lite` barrel + Havok + the nav plugin, i.e. scene252's load profile minus the scene/terrain.

How to read them:

- **recast-test finishes** (ends with `recast init done +…ms`) → the 2 MB glue module loads fine on its own, so the stall needs scene252's page context — two-wasm-test will show which ingredient (Havok, the barrel graph, or both) triggers it.
- **recast-test hangs at `glue`** → the module response itself is what this browser chokes on (my prime suspect now: the 2.07 MB response, most of it an inline base64 source map the dev server appends). The fix would be to strip that map from the served recast modules — I'll do that and you'd reload once more.

The on-page text is the channel this time (the console also works on the dev server, but the page text is unambiguous). If either page shows `ERROR:` or `REJECTION:` in red/green text, that's just as useful as a hang.

GOTCHA: Vite dev serves the excluded `@recast-navigation/*` modules (via `/@fs/`) with an **inline base64 source map** appended to the response — the served size is not the file size: the glue is 559 KB on disk but 2.07 MB served (`export default Recast;` ends at byte 559,665, the rest is the map); core is 102 KB→507 KB, generators 43 KB→206 KB — IMPLICATION: the stuck glue import is downloading ~1.5 MB of source map on top of the JS, so any size-based stall hypothesis must use served sizes, and the cheapest next experiment is stripping the inline source map (temp middleware) and checking whether the import then settles.
GOTCHA: `lab/vite.config.ts` has no sourcemap/inline setting — the inlining is Vite's default behavior for these `/@fs/`-served files, not a lab config choice — IMPLICATION: there is no existing config knob to disable it; shrinking the response requires a temporary middleware/plugin or serving the glue from `public/`.
GOTCHA: the glue module contains zero imports (no `import()`, no `from "..."`, no `require`) and ends cleanly on disk — IMPLICATION: the never-settling import can only be stalling on the network/fetch stage of the 2.07 MB response (or the browser's module loader), not on nested module evaluation, so the experiment should target the response payload itself, not the module graph.

DECISION: (confirmed) the Vite dev server serves these `/@fs/` node_modules modules with an inline base64 source map appended — served size is ~4–5× disk size (glue: 559 KB disk → 2.07 MB served; core: 102 KB → 507 KB; generators: 43 KB → 206 KB) — WHY: sha256 mismatch plus `sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64` at the tail, so the bloat is normal dev behavior, not a truncated/corrupt transform.

DECISION: (confirmed) the recast glue module is self-contained — zero import/require statements, ends `export default Recast;` — WHY: the stuck import therefore cannot be a nested module load; the hang is in delivery/evaluation of this single response.

DECISION: (confirmed) the stall is client-side, not server-side — WHY: the dev-server log is clean and curl fetches the full 2.07 MB in <200 ms, while the browser's import never settles (and never rejects — no error box, spinner still animating).

DECISION: (changed working hypothesis) the distinguishing factor is the ~2 MB served response size — core (507 KB served) and generators (206 KB served) settled in the browser but the glue (2.07 MB served) did not — WHY: the next experiment should be size-reduced delivery (strip/disable the inline source map for `@recast-navigation/*`, or a minimal test page) rather than more emscripten-glue instrumentation.

GOTCHA: Vite's dev server appends an inline base64 source map to the served JS modules — the recast glue is 559 KB on disk but 2.07 MB served (core 102 KB→507 KB, generators 43 KB→206 KB), and the lab config has no sourcemap setting controlling this (it's Vite default dev behavior) — IMPLICATION: browser-downloaded response size ≠ disk file size; any size-based diagnosis or fix must account for the map, and shrinking the glue response means stripping the map (temporary plugin/middleware or serving the file raw), not a config toggle that already exists.
GOTCHA: `HavokPhysics_es.js` (the Havok JS glue) is only 67 KB on disk / 283 KB served — the ~2 MB Havok load is the `.wasm` asset, not the JS module — IMPLICATION: my "two big wasm JS modules on one page" framing was wrong; the recast glue is the only large JS module response on the page, and it's the lone >1 MB module.
GOTCHA: the browser completed plain `fetch()` of the 2 MB `HavokPhysics.wasm` (200, twice) yet the 2.07 MB glue *module import* never settles — IMPLICATION: this is not a generic response-size cap; the stall is specific to the module-import path or a page-context race, so the size experiment must target the module response itself (strip the inline map) rather than assuming fetch and import share limits.
GOTCHA: the recast glue module has zero imports — a self-contained IIFE ending in `export default Recast;` — IMPLICATION: the hang cannot be a nested module load; the suspect list is exactly two (the response itself vs. the page context), which is the split my two test pages are built to answer.

CONSTRAINT: `lab/vite.config.ts` `optimizeDeps.exclude` must keep `@babylonjs/core`, `@babylonjs/loaders`, `@babylonjs/havok`, `@recast-navigation/core`, `@recast-navigation/generators`, `@recast-navigation/wasm` excluded — esbuild's dep optimizer can't process the wasm binaries / `?raw` WGSL imports these ship, and the config comment says un-excluding them causes a hung pre-bundle.
CONSTRAINT: The Vite dev server serves these excluded node_modules modules with an inline base64 source map appended, so served response size is 3.7–5× the on-disk file size (glue: 559 KB on disk → 2.07 MB served; core: 102 KB → 507 KB; generators: 43 KB → 206 KB) — any size-limit diagnosis or fix must account for served size, not disk size.

The recast glue import fails consistently across all test cases, including the stock scene170, so the issue isn't the two-wasm interaction—it's that the 2.07 MB module response won't complete in this browser while smaller modules and the 2 MB wasm fetch succeed. I'll strip the inline source map from the recast modules to shrink the response to 560 KB and verify the fix works.

args.content: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by isolation): the recast glue module import stalls in the user's browser on EVERY page (scene170 too — the "scene170 works" premise was never verified). Mechanism: Vite dev appends an inline base64 source map to every served module; the 560KB glue becomes a 2.07MB response that the constrained test browser (≈8s per-page window) never finishes, while ≤507KB modules and 2MB plain fetch() of HavokPhysics.wasm complete. Fix: serveRecastRawPlugin in lab/vite.config.ts — dev-server middleware serving @recast-navigation dist files raw from disk (all three are self-contained native ESM, zero imports, so no Vite rewrite needed). Verified served sizes now = disk sizes (102KB/43KB/560KB). Dev server bg_8cef3683 on :5182. NOTE: this also explains the original "recast streaming stall" — the glue never loaded, so instantiateStreaming was never reached; the force-arraybuffer patch in scene252.ts may now be unnecessary (recast-test.html uses the real streaming path and will confirm).

The fix is live. Please hard-reload these two pages in order and send both screenshots:

1. **`http://localhost:5182/lite/recast-test.html`** — this page has *no* patches at all (real `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`, no Havok). If it now ends with `recast init done +…ms`, the glue loads and the wasm compiles through the normal path — which would mean my `force-arraybuffer` patch was a red herring all along (the glue never even got to the wasm load before) and I can delete it.
2. **`http://localhost:5182/lite/scene252.html`** — still carries the patch + stage markers. If it gets past `nav-plugin` and the game comes up, we're done with the hang.

What changed: the dev server now serves the three recast modules raw from disk (560 KB glue instead of 2.07 MB — the bloat was an inline base64 source map Vite appends to every module). A hard reload matters because your browser may have cached the old 2 MB response.

Lint is running in the background on the config change; I'll report when it finishes.

GOTCHA: Vite dev appends an inline base64 source map to every served module (confirmed on both the recast glue and first-party `engine.ts`), and the separate `.map` URL also returns 200 — the served recast glue is 2.07 MB vs 559 KB on disk, ~72% of it map — IMPLICATION: the stall variable is served response size, and shrinking it requires bypassing the transform (raw serve, as `serveRecastRawPlugin` does); the map is added by Vite's response assembly, so a transform hook can't strip it.
GOTCHA: all three `@recast-navigation` dist files (core, generators, wasm glue) are self-contained native ESM with zero imports — IMPLICATION: raw bytes from disk are a drop-in module replacement (no import rewriting needed), which is what makes the raw-serve plugin safe.
GOTCHA: stock scene170 (recast-only) also hangs in your browser — the "scene170 works, scene252 doesn't" premise was never actually verified — IMPLICATION: the Havok→recast ordering / two-wasm-interaction hypothesis is dead; the recast glue module load stalls on every page in this browser, so load-order changes (parallel navPromise, force-arraybuffer patch) were treating the wrong bug.
GOTCHA: your browser has a hard ~8s per-page load window that can't be extended — IMPLICATION: fixes must reduce bytes/work inside the window (smaller responses), not add waits, retries, or instrumentation rounds that burn the window.
GOTCHA: `HavokPhysics_es.js` is 67 KB on disk (283 KB served) — the ~2 MB is the `HavokPhysics.wasm` asset, and that 2 MB `fetch()` completed fine while the 2.07 MB *module* response never settled — IMPLICATION: any response-size cap in this browser applies to module responses, not `fetch()` responses; the only oversized module in scene252's graph is the recast glue, so raw-serving just those three files is the minimal fix.

The step went as expected: the `configureServer` middleware intercepted the `/@fs/` recast URLs before Vite's own handler, the `+` characters in the pnpm store paths passed through URL→filesystem unharmed, and all three files served byte-identical to disk (102 KB / 43 KB / 560 KB, glue ending cleanly at `export default Recast;` with no map). The source-map-bloat discovery and the self-contained-ESM verification happened in the previous step and are already recorded. One item remains open rather than a discovery: the lint run (bg_b51e8b6c) is still in flight, so the config edit isn't typecheck-verified yet.

DECISION: The scene252 init hang is root-caused to Vite dev's inline base64 source map bloating the 560 KB recast glue module into a 2.07 MB response that the constrained test browser never finishes within its ~8 s per-page window — WHY: isolation pages (recast-test, two-wasm-test) and stock scene170 all stalled at the glue import while ≤507 KB modules and the 2 MB plain `fetch()` of HavokPhysics.wasm completed, ruling out the two-wasm / instantiateStreaming hypothesis.
DECISION: The permanent fix is `serveRecastRawPlugin` in `lab/vite.config.ts` — a dev-server middleware serving `@recast-navigation` dist files raw from disk, bypassing Vite's transform — WHY: all three dist files are self-contained native ESM with zero imports, so raw bytes are a drop-in replacement that shrinks the glue response from 2.07 MB to its 560 KB disk size.
DECISION: The `force-arraybuffer` `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` patch in scene252.ts is now presumed unnecessary and will be deleted if recast-test.html (which uses the real streaming path) completes — WHY: the glue never loaded before, so the "streaming stall" was a misdiagnosis of the import stall, and a global `WebAssembly` mutation is a workaround I don't want to keep if it isn't load-bearing.

CONSTRAINT: The lab's test browser has a ~8-second per-page load window; a module response that doesn't complete within it leaves the import pending forever (no rejection, no error) — so anything served to that browser must deliver within the window, and "no console error + spinner" means a stalled response, not a failed one.
CONSTRAINT: Vite dev appends an inline base64 source map to every served module (the 560 KB recast glue becomes a 2.07 MB response, which is what stalls the window) — the @recast-navigation dist files must keep being served raw via `serveRecastRawPlugin` in `lab/vite.config.ts`; removing the plugin or routing those files back through Vite's transform reintroduces the import stall on every recast page (scene170 included).
